dossier.summary: Marlowe and Pike is a 30-person accounting firm that does bookkeeping and tax for small businesses.

chapters.title: Why the close drags
chapters.summary: Owen Park lists the four places a close stalls: bank feeds, receipts, accruals and review.

chapters.title: Fix the feeds before the first of the month
chapters.summary: Rosa Lindqvist says most late closes start with bank feeds that were never reconciled mid-month.

chapters.title: A review checklist partners will use
chapters.summary: A one-page review checklist cut partner review from two days to half a day at Rosa's firm.

chapters.title: Questions: clients who send receipts late
chapters.summary: Questions on clients who send receipts late and on how to staff the last two days of the close.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: The checklist is one page. Partners do not read a close package, they look for what is different from last month, so the checklist asks only for that.

transcript.speaker: Owen
transcript.text: And that took review from two days to half a day?

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: At our firm, yes. It was not faster reading. It was fewer things to read.

data.book_title: Want the checklist set up for your firm?
data.book_text: Owen can walk you through the one-page checklist in 20 minutes and adapt it to your clients.

takeaways.title: Reconcile the bank feeds mid-month
takeaways.body: Most late closes started with bank feeds that were never reconciled mid-month. A check partway through the month gets ahead of the biggest source of delay.

takeaways.title: Give partners a one-page review checklist
takeaways.body: A one-page checklist cut partner review from two days to half a day at Rosa's firm. For a managing partner, that is time back in the last two days of the close.

takeaways.title: Plan for clients who send receipts late
takeaways.body: The questions at the end cover clients who send receipts late and how to staff the last two days of the close.
